p.i: Creduntne igitur illi invnicum Seruatorem Iesum, qui à sanctis, aut à se, aut alunde fœlicitatem aut salutem quærunt?

main_text.p: Non: Etsi enim verbo quidem eo Seruato-re gloriantur, reipsa tamen abnegant vnicum Seruatorem Iesum{2}. Necesse est enim aut Iesum non esse perfectum Seruatorem, aut qui eum Seruatorem vera fide amplectuntur, eos omnia in ipso possidere, quæ ad salutem requiruntur{b}.

p.i: Quare appellatur Christus, hoc est, vnctus?

main_text.p: Quód à Patre ordinatus, & Spiritu sancto vnctus sit{c} summus Propheta ac Doctor,{d} qui nobis arcanum consilium & omnem voluntatem Patris, de redemptione nostri patefecit{e}: & summus Pontifex,{f} qui nos vnico sacrificio sui corporis redemit, ac assidué pro nobis apud Patrem intercedit{g}: & Rex, qui nos suo verbo & Spiritu gubernat, & partam nobis salutem tuetur ac conseruat{h}.

Quód per fidem membrum sumus Iesu Chri-sti,{i} & vnctionis ipsius particeps{k}, vt & nomen eius confitear{l}, neque sistam ipsi viuam gratitudinis hostiam{m}, & in hac vita contra peccatum & Satanam, libera & bona conscientia pugnem, & postea æternum cum Christo regnum in omnes creaturas teneam{n}.

p.i: Quam ob causam Christus vocatur filius Dei vnigenitus, cum nos quoq; simus filii Dei?

page.notes: The marginal references are set in a small, tightly spaced type. Some letters are close together and a few are doubtful, notably "Ies" in note b (read as Ies for Ief), "Ioel" in note k, and the numbers in notes a and m. Where the letter shapes were uncertain I have transcribed them as printed without correction. The superscript reference letters in the text (b to n) have no matching footnotes visible on this part of the page. The sentence "sumus" in the membrum line is read from a damaged join and is doubtful. The phrase "viuam gratitudinis" has an unclear mark after "viuam" and may read differently.
